basics.name: Wai Shing Tang, Ph.D.
basics.label: Computational Biophysicist & AI Scientist
basics.summary: A computational biophysicist and AI scientist specialising in statistical modelling, generative machine learning, and high-performance computing. Experienced in designing Bayesian inference frameworks, diffusion-based generative models, and GPU-accelerated pipelines for structural biology and complex physical systems.

work.name: Self-Employed
work.position: Independent AI Scientist & Research Engineer Consultant
work.summary: Consulting on deep learning engineering and dynamical systems modeling for domain-specific applications.
highlights: Work with clients on AI research, machine learning engineering, and scientific data modelling projects across domains
Developed a prototype multi-modal transformer-based foundation model for cross-domain prediction and generation tasks.
Designed data pipelines, tokenization strategies, and deep learning components in PyTorch and JAX.

Developed uncertainty-aware dynamical models and Bayesian optimization algorithms for real-world telemetry and physical data analysis, integrating Bayesian inference, control theory, and machine learning.
Applied statistical modelling and machine learning methods to extract insights from complex, sparse, and high-dimensional temporal datasets to support data-driven decision-making.

work.name: Microsoft Research Cambridge
work.summary: Fixed-term research position developing diffusion-based generative models for protein structure. Departed October 2025 to take a planned health break.
highlights: Designed Bayesian inference frameworks and probabilistic models to incorporate large-scale, noisy cryo-EM data into diffusion generative models for protein structure prediction.
Collaborated with machine learning researchers and software engineers to implement scalable scientific computing workflows.

work.name: Flatiron Institute
work.summary: Led the development of accelerated Bayesian inference frameworks and high-performance software for processing cryo-EM datasets.
highlights: Led the development of Bayesian inference frameworks for extracting molecular structural information from highly noisy cryo-EM imaging data

Optimized likelihood-based inference algorithms using PyTorch and GPU-accelerated computing, achieving more than 20x acceleration over CPU baselines, enabling new Bayesian applications in biomolecular structure determination.
Integrated the algorithms into end-to-end software pipelines for processing and analyzing hundreds of TB of cryo-EM datasets across multiple GPUs on HPC.
Extended Bayesian inference approaches beyond cryo-EM to experimental chromatin datasets, developing methods to infer ensemble structural distributions from heterogeneous biological measurements.
Mentored junior researchers on Bayesian modelling, scientific machine learning, molecular dynamics simulations, and high-performance computational workflows.

work.name: Brown University
work.summary: Developed computational methods combining molecular simulation, statistical inference, and machine learning to study complex biomolecular systems.
highlights: Developed computational methods combining molecular simulation, statistical inference, and machine learning to study complex biomolecular systems.

Performed large-scale molecular dynamics simulations (using GROMACS and OpenMM) to investigate molecular interactions, conformational landscapes, and phase behavior of intrinsically disordered proteins.

Applied advanced enhanced sampling methods (including REMD (Replica Exchange Molecular Dynamics) and PT-WTE (Parallel Tempering Well-Tempered Ensemble)) to characterize rare conformational states and molecular mechanisms.

Developed Gaussian process-based feature selection and topological data analysis approaches to extract meaningful structural representations and identify structural features distinguishing protein variants and predict mutational effects from short (<200 ns) MD simulation trajectories.
Built scalable HPC workflows for molecular simulation, trajectory analysis, and large-scale scientific data processing.

courses: Thesis: Topological Data Analysis framework for biological structures and short-term evolving molecular models

publications.name: Ensemble Reweighting Using Cryo-EM Particle Images
publications.publisher: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
publications.summary: Establishes a novel statistical reweighting framework for structural ensembles using single-particle cryo-EM datasets. [Stack: Python, Bayesian Reweighting, Conformational Heterogeneity, Cryo-EM Particle Analysis]

publications.name: Conformational heterogeneity and probability distributions from single-particle cryo-electron microscopy
publications.summary: Reviews emerging methods for determining conformational landscapes and probability distributions of macromolecules from single-particle cryo-EM. [Keywords: Single-Particle Cryo-EM, Structural Ensemble Analysis, Probability Modeling]

publications.name: A topological data analytic approach for discovering biophysical signatures in protein dynamics
publications.summary: Introduces a topological summary statistics framework to identify biophysical features distinguishing conformational differences in molecular trajectories. [Stack: Python, Topological Data Analysis, Gaussian Processes, Feature Selection]

publications.name: Molecular interactions contributing to FUS SYGQ LC-RGG phase separation and co-partitioning with RNA polymerase II heptads
